Download NOAA High-Resolution Rapid Refresh (HRRR) data

Source: R/source-hrrr.R
download_hrrr.Rd

Downloads NOAA High-Resolution Rapid Refresh (HRRR) model data from the NOAA HRRR public Amazon S3 archive.

The function supports the HRRR three-dimensional pressure-level, native-level, two-dimensional surface, and sub-hourly products. Select one product per call, with multiple dates, model cycle run times, and forecast hours if needed.

HRRR data are downloaded as GRIB2 files and organized under a sector-specific directory within directory_to_save.

Usage

download_hrrr(
  product = NULL,
  sector = "conus",
  date = c("2018-01-01", "2018-01-01"),
  cycle_runtime = 0:23,
  forecast_hour = 0:18,
  directory_to_save = NULL,
  acknowledgement = FALSE,
  download = TRUE,
  remove_command = FALSE,
  show_progress = TRUE,
  hash = FALSE,
  max_tries = 20,
  rate_limit = 2
)

Arguments

product

character(1). Required HRRR product to download. Accepted values are "3d pressure", "native", "2d surface", "sub-hourly", or "subhourly". Matching is case-insensitive. The default NULL must be replaced with a product name.

sector

character(1). HRRR geographic sector to download. Currently only "conus" is supported and is the default. Matching is case-insensitive.

date

character(1 or 2). Dates in "YYYY-MM-DD" format defining the download period. A single date downloads data for that date. When two dates are supplied, all dates from the earlier date through the later date are included. All dates must be between "2014-07-30" and today, inclusive. Dates outside this range raise an error before directory creation or network requests.

cycle_runtime

numeric vector. Non-missing model initialization hour(s), specified as whole numbers from 0 through 23. Defaults to 0:23. Values are formatted as two-digit UTC cycle times when constructing the HRRR file names. At least one hour is required; repeated hours are requested once.

forecast_hour

numeric vector. Non-missing forecast lead hour(s), specified as whole numbers from 0 through 48. Defaults to 0:18, including the zero-hour lead (f00) at the model initialization time. Values are formatted as two-digit forecast hours when constructing the HRRR file names. At least one hour is required; repeated hours are requested once.

directory_to_save

character(1). Required non-empty directory path for downloaded HRRR files. Missing parent directories and the sector-specific subdirectory are created automatically.

acknowledgement

logical(1). Must be TRUE to acknowledge the download before data are retrieved.

download

logical(1). Deprecated. FALSE emits a warning and returns a download preview. Argument validation, directory creation, and URL construction still run before returning.

remove_command

logical(1). Deprecated and ignored. TRUE emits a warning.

show_progress

logical(1). Show per-file messages and progress bars during sequential downloads. Defaults to TRUE. Ignored during concurrent downloads, where per-file progress is disabled. Status and summary messages may still be printed when FALSE.

hash

logical(1). Return a combined MD5 hash of all files recursively under directory_to_save, including existing files, instead of the download summary. Defaults to FALSE.

max_tries

integer(1). Maximum attempts per file request, including the initial attempt. Must be at least 1. Defaults to 20.

rate_limit

numeric(1). Finite, non-negative request-throttling interval in seconds. Defaults to 2. Passed unchanged to download_run_method() for sequential downloads. For concurrent downloads, multiplied by the configured daemon count for the "default" compute profile before being passed to each worker.

Value

If hash = FALSE, an invisible summary from download_run() containing success, failed, skipped, failed_urls, and failed_files. The two failure vectors are character(0) when no downloads failed, including when every file was skipped. If hash = TRUE, a visible character scalar containing the combined MD5 hash of all files recursively under directory_to_save, including existing files.

Details

Dates select model initialization days. Each selected cycle run time and forecast hour is requested for every date. URLs are constructed directly; validation does not check whether each requested product, cycle, and forecast hour is available in the archive.

Product names map to the file codes prs (3d pressure), nat (native), sfc (2d surface), and subh (either sub-hourly spelling). Local filenames include the initialization date to distinguish files from different days. For example, surface data initialized at 12 UTC on January 1, 2020, with a one-hour forecast lead are saved as conus/hrrr.20200101.t12z.wrfsfcf01.grib2 under directory_to_save.

Downloads use download_run(), which skips existing non-empty destination files. Handled download failures are recorded in the returned summary and reported with a warning. See that helper for concurrent download setup and worker requirements.

Note

No authentication token is required for this public archive.

Concurrent downloads

File downloads use caller-configured mirai::daemons() in the "default" compute profile, or run sequentially when that profile has no daemons. Configure a fixed pool with mirai::daemons(n, .compute = "default") before calling this function. The caller manages pool creation and shutdown; keep the pool size unchanged during downloads.

Workers need compatible amadeus code and its dependencies, plus access to the same destination storage as the calling process. Loading development code in the calling process does not load it on workers; use mirai::everywhere() to load the same code on workers when needed. Validation, URL construction, directory setup, and hashing run in the calling process. Only file downloads are dispatched to workers.

See also

download_run(), sequence_dates()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
download_hrrr(
  product = "2d surface",
  sector = "conus",
  date = "2020-01-01",
  cycle_runtime = 12,
  forecast_hour = 1:18,
  directory_to_save = tempdir(),
  acknowledgement = TRUE
)

download_hrrr(
  product = "sub-hourly",
  date = c("2020-01-01", "2020-01-03"),
  cycle_runtime = 0:23,
  forecast_hour = 1:6,
  directory_to_save = tempdir(),
  acknowledgement = TRUE
)
} # }
